issues.legal_issue: Rule 19 of the Development Control Rules has the force of law.
Rule 19 of the Development Control Rules is within the authority conferred by the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act.
The requirement to reserve and transfer open-space land for communal and recreational purposes does not violate Article 14 of the Constitution.
The requirement to reserve and transfer open-space land for communal and recreational purposes does not violate Article 300A of the Constitution.
The requirement to reserve open-space land under the planning rules is distinct from the land reservation and acquisition provisions in Sections 36 and 37 of the Act.
The open-space requirement does not entitle a developer to compensation under Section 39 of the Act.
The challenged planning rules and regulations are not invalid for being inconsistent with Sections 48 to 55 of the Act.
Open-space reservation land must be used only for communal and recreational purposes and cannot be diverted to other uses.
The term communal and recreational purposes permits members of the general public to access open-space reservation land in developments exceeding 10,000 square metres.
